lesson.title: Biometric identity
lesson.summary: Distinguish identity verification from remote identification using technical and interaction facts.

prerequisites.reason: The data definition is introduced in the context of identifying inputs used by the system.

blocks: **Biometric data** result from specific technical processing of physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics. A facial image used for such processing can be relevant; do not treat every photograph as the same processing activity.
Northbridge's fictional access desk uses a face comparison. Record the processed characteristic, purpose and reference data before deciding which identity test is being used.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(34)–(36), 3(41); Annex III 1(a)

blocks: **Biometric verification** is one-to-one confirmation of a person's claimed identity. Identification seeks to establish identity through comparison with stored individuals. Ask whether the question is 'Are you the person you claim to be?' or 'Who is this person?'

A person actively confirming their identity against their own enrolled record differs from searching an unknown visitor against many records. The purpose and comparison matter more than the word 'login'.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(34)–(36), 3(41); Annex III 1(a)

blocks: **Remote biometric identification** identifies people without their active involvement, typically at a distance, by comparing biometric data with a reference database. Distance alone is not the complete definition.
An entrance camera identifying passers-by against a reference database illustrates facts relevant to the remote test. Record involvement, matching process and intended identity purpose.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(34)–(36), 3(41); Annex III 1(a)

blocks: Annex III 1(a) lists remote biometric identification, where use is otherwise permitted by law. It excludes verification whose sole purpose is confirming the specific person's claimed identity.
That point-specific exclusion does not make every verification use free of every AI Act or privacy duty. Article 5's separate real-time/public-space/law-enforcement rule will be taught later.

questions.prompt: A user claims one identity and actively confirms it against their own enrolled record only. Which distinction fits?

options.blocks: Finding an unknown person among many records
options.reason: That describes identification rather than the stated sole verification purpose.
Emotion inference is a different purpose.

options.blocks: Confirming the person is who they claim to be
options.reason: That is the verification definition and the specific Annex III limit.
